explanation: UFO researchers (Allan Hendry, Jerome Clark) consider it significant. Skeptic Philip Klass argued it was a hoax and that Johnson damaged the car himself. The patrol car is on display at the Marshall County museum.
shape: Beam of bright light just above the road
witnesses: 1 (Deputy Sheriff Val Johnson)
summary: Deputy Val Johnson was patrolling rural roads when he saw a bright light just above the road. It rushed toward his car, the car was engulfed in light, and he heard glass breaking. He said he was unconscious for 39 minutes. Deputies found the car skewed across the road. The windshield was cracked, a headlight and the roof light were broken, and an aerial was bent. Both his watch and the car's clock were 14 minutes slow. A doctor compared his eye irritation to "welder's burns".

title: Dechmont Law — Robert Taylor
shape: Dome-shaped object; two spiked spheres
witnesses: 1 (forester Robert Taylor)
summary: Forestry worker Robert Taylor walked into a clearing on Dechmont Law and saw a large dome-shaped object hovering. He said two smaller spiked spheres rolled out, grabbed his trousers and dragged him toward it, and he passed out. He came to with torn trousers, grazes and a headache, and staggered home. Police recorded the case as an assault and found marks in the ground. It is often described as the only UFO event police have investigated as a crime. A marker now stands at the site.

title: Manises — airliner diversion & Mirage intercept
explanation: Spanish Air Force files declassified in the 1990s did not confirm an anomalous object; researchers attribute the lights to refinery flare stacks and bright stars/planets.
shape: Red lights on a collision course; truncated cone
witnesses: TAE crew, 109 passengers, controllers, Mirage pilot
summary: TAE flight JK-297 from Salzburg (via Palma) to Las Palmas saw red lights approach on a collision course near Ibiza and track the aircraft after it changed altitude. The captain diverted to Valencia — the first airliner diverted by a UFO. A Mirage F1 from Los Llanos then chased lights that accelerated away.

title: La Joya air base pursuit
place: La Joya air base, Arequipa, Peru
explanation: Peru’s air force kept the case quiet for decades; no explanation has been published. Peru has since set up an office (now DIFAA) for aerial anomalies, and U.S. documents on the case were later released.
shape: Large balloon-shaped object
witnesses: Lt Oscar Santa María Huertas; some 1,800 people at the base
summary: On the morning of April 11, 1980 about 1,800 people at the La Joya base saw a large, balloon-shaped object hanging still at around 500 metres. Lt Oscar Santa María Huertas, 23, took off in a Sukhoi Su-22 and fired 64 rounds at it without effect. He reported that it climbed away at up to 950 km/h, reaching about 19,200 metres, and stopped so suddenly that he had to swerve to avoid it. Peruvian army radar was said to show only his aircraft, while operators saw the object by eye. The engagement is said to have lasted 22 minutes, until his fuel ran low. The Peruvian Air Force kept the matter classified for decades; U.S. defence documents titled “UFO sighted in Peru” have since been released.

title: Todmorden — PC Alan Godfrey
shape: Diamond-shaped object hovering over the road
witnesses: PC Alan Godfrey; other officers saw a light that night
summary: Before dawn, PC Alan Godfrey was driving his patrol car along Burnley Road looking for missing cattle when he found a large, diamond-shaped object hovering about 5 ft above the road, blocking it. He sketched it from the car. The next thing he knew, he was farther down the road and some time had passed. He said the road surface under the object was dry though the rest was wet. Other officers reported a light in the sky that night. Later hypnosis sessions produced an abduction account.

title: Rendlesham Forest
place: Rendlesham Forest, outside RAF Woodbridge, Suffolk
explanation: The Ministry of Defence found no threat and did not investigate further. Skeptics attribute the lights to a fireball, the Orford Ness lighthouse (visible through the trees in the same direction) and bright stars.
shape: Metallic lit object in the forest; star-like lights
witnesses: USAF security police; Lt. Col. Charles Halt
summary: USAF security patrols at the east gate of RAF Woodbridge saw lights descend into the forest and went in to investigate. Two nights later deputy base commander Lt. Col. Charles Halt led a team that took radiation readings at three ground depressions and recorded his observations on a micro-cassette. His memo to the MoD is one of the most famous UFO documents in Britain.

title: Cash–Landrum incident
explanation: Army and Air Force inquiries found no helicopters or craft that matched; the witnesses’ lawsuit against the U.S. government was dismissed in 1986. Skeptics question the medical and helicopter claims.
shape: Diamond-shaped object venting flame; escorted by ~23 helicopters
witnesses: Betty Cash, Vickie & Colby Landrum; other motorists
summary: Driving home through the pine woods north-east of Houston, Betty Cash and Vickie Landrum with her grandson said a blazing diamond-shaped object hovered over the road, radiating heat. As it rose, they counted about two dozen helicopters, many resembling CH-47 Chinooks. All three reported injuries afterwards, and they sued the U.S. government.

title: Trans-en-Provence landing trace
explanation: The French government’s GEPAN (now GEIPAN, part of CNES) analysed soil and plant samples and reported heating and biochemical changes it could not attribute to a known cause. Skeptics suggest a vehicle or the witness.
shape: Lead-grey disc, two stacked saucers
witnesses: Renato Nicolaï
summary: Renato Nicolaï heard a whistle and saw an object land briefly on his terrace and fly off. The Gendarmerie took samples within a day; GEPAN’s laboratory analysis of the 2.4 m circular mark reported soil heated to 300–600 °C and chlorophyll changes in alfalfa leaves.

title: Morenão stadium sighting
place: Estádio Morenão, Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul
shape: Unidentified lights
witnesses: More than 24,000 spectators, players and the referee
summary: During a Brazilian championship match between Operário and Vasco da Gama, a crowd of more than 24,000 saw unidentified objects over the stadium. Players, including Cocada, and referee José de Assis Aragão described them. Among the spectators was Ademar José Gevaerd, who went on to become one of Brazil's best-known UFO researchers.

title: Hessdalen lights
explanation: Studied since 1983 by Project Hessdalen with an automated measurement station; hypotheses include combustion of dust from the valley’s ores, plasma, and piezoelectric effects.
shape: White, yellow or red floating lights
witnesses: Residents and scientists
summary: Lights have appeared over the 12-km Hessdalen valley since at least the early 1980s, peaking at up to 20 per week in 1981–84. Unusually, they have been measured: radar, spectra, magnetometers and a permanent camera station have recorded them, but their cause is still debated.

title: Hudson Valley "Westchester boomerang"
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: State police and the New York Power Authority attributed the sightings to pilots flying Cessna 152s in tight formation from Stormville Airport with coloured lights — a hoax the pilots reportedly enjoyed.
shape: V / boomerang of coloured lights
witnesses: Thousands across Westchester, Putnam, Dutchess and Fairfield counties
summary: For over a year residents of the Hudson Valley reported a silent boomerang or V of bright lights, sometimes "the size of a football field". Guards at the Indian Point nuclear plant reportedly saw it in June and July 1984, and a Brewster resident videotaped the lights on 24 July.

title: Dalnegorsk “Height 611” crash
explanation: Ball lightning and other plasma phenomena have been proposed. The reports of unusual metal fragments come mostly from the investigating group and have not been independently confirmed.
shape: Reddish sphere about 3 m across
witnesses: Residents of Dalnegorsk
summary: On the evening of January 29, 1986 residents of the mining town of Dalnegorsk saw a reddish, silent sphere about three metres across flying from the south-east at some 700–800 metres, at about 15 m/s. It crossed part of the town and came down on Izvestkovaya mountain, known as Height 611, burning on the slope. Investigators reported tiny metallic droplets 2–5 mm across, and fibres in a tangle of metal, quartz and gold-coloured threads. In Russia it is often called the best-documented UFO crash, although the technical findings come mainly from the group that investigated it.

title: Brazil’s "Official UFO Night"
place: São José dos Campos – Rio de Janeiro – Goiás
explanation: The Air Force commander said "we have no explanation". The report declassified in 2009 described objects with speeds from hovering to supersonic and 90° turns.
shape: Red, white and green lights; 21 radar plots
witnesses: Controllers, F-5E and Mirage pilots, Embraer founder Ozires Silva
summary: Controllers at São José dos Campos and radar across south-east Brazil tracked about 21 unknown contacts. Embraer’s founder, flying in, saw red lights; the Air Force scrambled F-5Es from Santa Cruz and Mirage IIIs from Anápolis. Pilots reported lights that kept their distance and targets that appeared behind them.

title: Torpo film
shape: Two bright objects, one flashing and throwing sparks
witnesses: A family and friends at a mountain farm
summary: A couple at a mountain farm near Torpo, with their son and friends, watched two bright objects in the evening sky, one moving dramatically, flashing and throwing off sparks. The husband filmed them. Ground Saucer Watch found no sign of a hoax, but said the apparent motion could come from camera shake and that the lack of reference points made the film inconclusive.

title: Japan Air Lines Flight 1628
explanation: The FAA’s radar returns were later dismissed as clutter / a split image; Philip Klass argued the crew saw Jupiter and Mars. The FAA found the crew professional and rational.
shape: Two small lights and a huge "mothership"
witnesses: Capt. Kenji Terauchi and crew
summary: A JAL Boeing 747 freighter on the Reykjavík–Anchorage leg reported three objects pacing it at 35,000 ft, including one Terauchi described as enormous. Anchorage controllers reported returns near the aircraft; the objects stayed with the plane through turns and descents until near Talkeetna.

title: Gulf Breeze photographs
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: Considered a hoax. In 1990 the new owners of Ed Walters's former house found a styrofoam model UFO in the attic that a reporter used to reproduce the photos almost exactly. A local teenager also said he had helped fake them. Walters said the model was planted.
shape: Cylindrical craft with a ring of portholes and a glowing base
witnesses: Ed Walters; other residents later came forward
summary: Contractor Ed Walters gave the Gulf Breeze Sentinel five Polaroids of a glowing craft he said hovered near his home. Over six months he produced dozens more photos and video, and described being hit by a blue beam and seeing aliens. Researchers such as Bruce Maccabee backed the photos, and other residents reported sightings. After the model was found in 1990 and a reporter recreated the pictures, the case became a textbook example of a UFO photo hoax.

title: Ilkley Moor photograph
explanation: Critics say the blurry photograph could show a person or a cardboard cutout, and ask why no picture of the craft was taken. Kodak experts found no sign of tampering, but the image is too grainy for firm conclusions, and the account changed under hypnosis.
shape: Small green humanoid; two-part silver craft
witnesses: Philip Spencer, a retired police officer (a pseudonym)
duration: Minutes; about two hours unaccounted for
summary: On the morning of December 1, 1987 Philip Spencer, a retired police officer, was walking across Ilkley Moor, between Ilkley and Keighley, when he said he met a small dark-green figure about 1.2 metres tall, with a large head and long thin arms. He took one photograph before it ran off, then saw a whitish, two-part craft rise from the moor with a loud hum. About two hours were missing from his journey, and his compass pointed the wrong way. A wildlife photographer said the figure matched no known animal and Kodak found no signs of tampering, but the US Navy optics specialist Bruce Maccabee called the image too grainy to test. Under hypnosis in March 1988 his story changed to one of being taken aboard and examined.

title: Knowles family encounter
place: Nullarbor Plain, between Madura and Mundrabilla, Western Australia
explanation: No explanation has been established. The account rests on the four family members’ testimony and the physical details they described, and has been widely reported in Australia.
shape: Large glowing ball
witnesses: Faye Knowles and her sons Patrick, Sean and Wayne
summary: In the early hours of January 20, 1988, the Knowles family were driving across the Nullarbor Plain in their station wagon when a bright light appeared ahead. They said a large glowing object pursued the car for a long time and finally came down on the roof; the car seemed to be lifted off the road, and the engine and voices changed as if time were slowing. Mrs Knowles said she reached out of the rear window, felt something soft and warm on the roof, and found her hand covered in black dust. When the car dropped back onto the road a rear tyre burst. The family reported it at Mundrabilla. It is one of Australia’s best-known close-encounter stories.

title: Villa Urquiza Christmas sighting
shape: Silver object
witnesses: More than 7,500
summary: On Christmas Day 1988 a silver object crossed the Villa Urquiza neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, watched by thousands of people. The city airport reported an object heading west toward Avenida General Paz. It is often called Argentina's most spectacular UFO sighting.

title: Voronezh park landing
explanation: Reported by the Soviet news agency TASS; later widely regarded as a children’s story amplified by the press.
shape: Large red sphere / oval
witnesses: Mainly children in a city park
summary: TASS reported that children in a Voronezh park saw a large red ball land and tall beings emerge. Soviet reporting of the case — unusual at the time — made headlines worldwide.

title: Belgian UFO wave — F-16 intercepts
explanation: The Belgian Air Force report left the radar contacts unexplained; critics attribute the F-16 lock-ons to the other fighter and to Bragg scattering. The famous Petit-Rechain triangle photo was admitted to be a hoax in 2011.
shape: Dark triangle with bright corner lights
witnesses: ~13,500 reports in the wave; gendarmes; Air Force
summary: Beginning with a sighting by two gendarmes at Eupen on 29 November 1989, thousands of Belgians reported large, slow triangles with lights. On the night of 30–31 March 1990, after ground and radar reports, two Belgian Air Force F-16s from Beauvechain made nine interception attempts and obtained brief radar locks; the Air Force published its report openly.

title: Calvine photograph
explanation: The MoD never explained it; proposed explanations include a rock reflected in water and a hoax. The photographers have never been identified.
shape: Large diamond hovering; a Harrier jet nearby
witnesses: Two unidentified walkers
summary: Two men walking above Calvine photographed a large, silent diamond-shaped object hovering while a military jet flew past. Their negatives went from the Daily Record to the Ministry of Defence and vanished. A surviving print surfaced in 2022 and was published worldwide.

title: Montreal — lights over the Bonaventure Hotel
shape: Ring of 8–10 bright lights; a huge round form
witnesses: Hotel guests and staff, passers-by, police officers
summary: From 7:20 to 10:20 p.m., people on the rooftop pool deck of the Bonaventure Hotel and in the streets below watched 8 to 10 lights hanging in a circle above them, sending down bright white rays. Some described a huge round object behind the lights. Police officers attended, and the next day La Presse reported the sighting. It drifted slowly north and was never identified.

title: Alitalia MD-80 near miss over Kent
explanation: The Civil Aviation Authority and the Ministry of Defence looked at missiles, weather balloons and rockets and ruled each one out, then closed the inquiry without an answer. The files were released by the National Archives in October 2008.
shape: Brown, missile-shaped object
witnesses: Capt. Achille Zaghetti, with 57 people aboard
summary: At about 8 p.m. on April 21, 1991, an Alitalia MD-80 flying from Milan to Heathrow with 57 people aboard was at 22,000 feet over the army ranges at Lydd, on the Kent coast, when Capt. Achille Zaghetti saw a brown, missile-shaped object pass about 1,000 feet above the airliner and shouted “Look out, look out”. The London control centre told him it had an unknown target on radar 10 nautical miles behind him. The Ministry of Defence and the Civil Aviation Authority investigated as an airmiss, ruled out a missile, a weather balloon and a rocket, and closed the case unsolved.

title: Mexico City eclipse videos
explanation: Astronomers identified the brightest object as Venus (with Mars and Regulus nearby), made visible by the darkness of totality. Reflections in glass, camera artefacts and hoaxes account for others; not every video has been explained.
shape: Metallic disc or bright point, sometimes with a wavy haze
witnesses: Dozens of video and photo recordings by different people
summary: Millions in Mexico watched the total solar eclipse of July 11, 1991, with totality in Mexico City at 13:24 and lasting more than six minutes. At least 16 photographers and videographers recorded a bright, disc-like object near the Sun in the sky, some with a wavy trail of haze behind it. The sightings were widely seen on television and the case is a classic in Mexican ufology. Astronomers pointed out that the darkness of totality shows Venus, which stood a few degrees from the star Regulus, and that other planets also come into view, which fits many of the videos but not necessarily the apparent motion some of them show.

title: Cosford incident
place: RAF Cosford and RAF Shawbury, Shropshire
explanation: Most of the evening reports matched the re-entry of the rocket body that had launched the Russian satellite Cosmos 2238. The MoD found no threat. Nick Pope, who investigated for the MoD, argued that later reports, including a meteorological officer's at RAF Shawbury, were never explained.
shape: Triangular craft; lights in formation
witnesses: Police officers, RAF personnel, members of the public
summary: Over the night of March 30–31, 1993, police officers, RAF personnel and the public across England and Wales reported lights in formation and a large triangular craft. A patrol at RAF Cosford saw it pass over the base. At RAF Shawbury a meteorological officer described a huge craft moving slowly across the airfield and sweeping a light beam over the ground. The MoD's Nick Pope pressed the case internally, and the files were later released to The National Archives.

title: Air France 3532 — radar-visual over Coulommiers
explanation: GEIPAN, the French space agency’s UAP office, classes the case as unexplained after investigation. The military radar track is real but does not match the crew’s account closely: the crew saw a stationary object far off to the left, while the radar target was about a mile to the right and moving. Both vanished at the same moment.
shape: Huge brown or dark-red disc or bell that seemed to change shape
witnesses: Capt. Jean-Charles Duboc, First Officer Valérie Chauffour and a chief steward
summary: At 13:14 on January 28, 1994, the crew of Air France flight 3532, an Airbus A320 from Nice to London, was cruising at about 11,900 metres near Coulommiers, east of Paris, when the chief steward and both pilots saw a huge object, like a brown bell or disc, off to the left. It seemed to change shape, stayed in view for about a minute and then vanished abruptly. Reims air traffic control had no traffic there, but the military radar at Cinq-Mars-la-Pile recorded a track for about 50 seconds that crossed the airliner’s path and disappeared at the same moment the crew lost sight of the object. The radar return and the crew’s description do not agree on distance or side, which is part of why the case remains open.

title: Ariel School, Ruwa
explanation: Skeptics suggest mass suggestion after a meteor/re-entry seen across southern Africa two days earlier; many former pupils still stand by their accounts.
shape: Silver craft landing in scrub; small beings
witnesses: 62 pupils aged 5–12
summary: During morning break, 62 children said a silver craft landed in bush beside the playground and one or two small figures in black watched them. Their drawings were collected within days, and Harvard psychiatrist John Mack interviewed them.

title: British Airways 5061 near miss over the Pennines
place: About 8 nautical miles south-east of Manchester Airport
explanation: The Civil Aviation Authority’s Joint Airmiss Working Group could not identify the object and rated the airmiss “unassessable”. No other aircraft or balloon was found, and no radar return was seen.
shape: Wedge-shaped object with small white lights and a black stripe
witnesses: Capt. Roger Wills and First Officer Mark Stuart
summary: At 18:48 on January 6, 1995, British Airways flight 5061, a Boeing 737 from Milan with 60 passengers aboard, was descending through about 4,000 feet over the Pennines toward Manchester when both pilots saw a lighted object pass very close down the right side, going the other way. They described it as wedge-shaped, with small white lights and a black stripe; the first officer ducked as it went by. Nothing showed on radar. The Joint Airmiss Working Group studied the report and, unable to identify the object, called it “unassessable”.

title: Bariloche — the blackout and Aerolíneas Argentinas 674
place: San Carlos de Bariloche airport, Río Negro, Argentina
explanation: No explanation was found. Carlos Angueira, president of a local astronomy association, rejected a meteorite or a refraction, saying such things cannot “stop in the middle of the sky”. The case drew new attention in 2026, when it appeared among the Latin American incidents in UAP files released by the Pentagon.
shape: A light between white and amber, like a star but much larger; later described as green and white, about 30 m across
witnesses: Capt. Jorge Polanco, his crew and passengers; the tower chief, Daniel García; the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne
summary: At about 8:15 p.m. on July 31, 1995, Aerolíneas Argentinas flight 674, a Boeing 727 from Buenos Aires under Capt. Jorge Polanco, was coming in to land at Bariloche when the airport lost power, and then the whole city went dark as the airliner neared the runway, forcing a go-around. A light “between white and amber”, like a star but much larger and brighter, then flew on a parallel course about 100 metres from the plane. When the power came back the 727 climbed to 3,000 metres, descended and landed, and the light left at full speed toward the south-east. The tower chief and the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne flying 600 metres higher saw it too, and the tower’s instruments swung from one direction to another for no clear reason. Interviewed in 2026, Polanco said: “It pursued us, accompanied us for 17 minutes.”

title: Varginha "ET"
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: A Brazilian Army inquiry concluded that the women had seen a local man with a mental disability, known as "Mudinho", and that the military movements were routine.
shape: Crouching humanoid with red eyes
witnesses: 3 young women; later many rumours
summary: Three young women said they saw a strange creature crouched near a wall, with vein-like marks on its skin, three bumps on its head and eyes like "two red balls". Rumours followed of military trucks carrying captured beings, bodies at hospitals, a police officer's death and animal deaths at the zoo. It became Brazil's best-known UFO story and a local tourist theme.

title: Pretoria police helicopter chase
shape: Bright, colour-changing light
witnesses: About 200 police officers; helicopter crew
summary: At 4 a.m., Sgt Nico Stander of the Adriaan Vlok police station in Pretoria reported lights in the sky, which were videotaped. Some 200 officers and a Bo-105 police helicopter followed them east. The helicopter gave up at about 10,000 ft over the Cullinan area when it ran low on fuel. The lights were seen again on the nights of August 31 and September 1.

title: The Wash incident
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: The radar returns were at least partly explained as echoes from St Botolph's Church ("the Boston Stump"), and the visual sightings as stars and planets.
shape: Rotating, multicoloured light
witnesses: Police officer David Leyland; other witnesses
summary: In the early morning a police officer on the Lincolnshire coast reported a rotating, multicoloured object over The Wash. The Claxby air traffic control radar reported a return in the same area. The report went up through RAF Kinloss and MoD Northwood before the conventional explanation was accepted.

title: Phoenix Lights
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: The ~20:00–20:45 V-formation was traced to A-10 aircraft of Operation Snowbird returning to Davis-Monthan AFB; the ~22:00 row of lights filmed over Phoenix were LUU-2 flares dropped over the Barry Goldwater Range. Some witnesses, including then-governor Fife Symington, reject this.
shape: Huge V / carpenter’s square with five lights
witnesses: Thousands along a 300-mile corridor
summary: A V-shaped formation of lights was reported moving south-east from the Nevada line, over Prescott Valley and Phoenix to Tucson. Later that night a stationary row of amber lights was widely filmed over Phoenix. The event remains one of the most-witnessed UFO events in U.S. history.

title: Southern Illinois police sightings
explanation: The FAA suggested an advertising blimp; the officers’ descriptions of speed and size are hard to reconcile with that.
shape: Huge triangle / "arrowhead" with bright lights
witnesses: 5 police officers in 4 towns, a store owner
summary: Before dawn, a store owner in Highland and then police officers in Lebanon, Summerfield, Shiloh and Dupo independently reported a large, low triangular object with bright lights moving south-west toward Scott AFB and the Mississippi.

title: Mexican Air Force FLIR — Campeche
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: Most analysts identified the lights as gas flares on Cantarell offshore oil platforms seen over the horizon by the infrared camera.
shape: 11 bright infrared lights
witnesses: Mexican Air Force Merlin C-26A crew
summary: A Mexican Air Force surveillance aircraft hunting drug flights recorded 11 bright objects on its infrared camera at about 11,500 ft. The Defence Department released the tape on 12 May 2004.

title: Tinley Park lights
place: Tinley Park and Oak Forest, Illinois
explanation: Commonly attributed to balloons or kites carrying lights or flares, which match the slow drift and the colour. No one has come forward, and the cause has not been confirmed.
shape: Three to four red lights in a triangle
witnesses: Hundreds in the south suburbs of Chicago
summary: On the evening of August 21, 2004, hundreds of people in Chicago's south suburbs watched three large red lights in a triangle drift slowly and silently across the sky. Many filmed them. The lights returned on October 31, 2004 and on several nights in 2005 and 2006, and appeared on national television. They are a prominent "black triangle" style case with plenty of video.

title: USS Nimitz "Tic Tac"
place: Pacific Ocean ~100 mi SW of San Diego
explanation: The Pentagon released the FLIR1 video in 2020 and describes the object as unidentified. Skeptics argue the FLIR clip shows a distant aircraft; the pilots’ visual account is independent of the video.
evidence: video | sensor-data | radar | pilot-witness | military-witness | official-document
shape: White, smooth 40-ft "Tic Tac"
witnesses: 4 aircrew (Fravor, Dietrich + WSOs), USS Princeton radar operators
summary: For days the cruiser USS Princeton’s SPY-1 radar tracked objects appearing at about 80,000 ft, dropping rapidly toward the sea and hovering. On 14 November, Cdr. David Fravor and Lt. Cdr. Alex Dietrich were vectored to a contact and saw a white Tic Tac-shaped object above a churning patch of ocean. It mirrored Fravor’s descent, then accelerated away; seconds later Princeton reported it at the pilots’ CAP point ~60 miles away. A later sortie filmed the FLIR1 video.

title: Chicago O’Hare disc
explanation: The FAA called it a "weather phenomenon" and did not investigate; conditions suited a hole-punch cloud. Nothing appeared on radar.
shape: Dark grey metallic disc, 6–24 ft
witnesses: ~12 United Airlines employees; people outside the airport
summary: A ramp worker pushing back United Flight 446 saw a dark disc hovering low over Gate C-17; pilots, supervisors and mechanics came out to watch. Witnesses said it shot straight up through the overcast, leaving a clear hole in the clouds that closed moments later. The story emerged via a Chicago Tribune FOIA request.

title: Alderney airline sighting
explanation: Jersey radar showed only a faint primary return; proposed explanations include earthquake lights and sun dogs.
shape: Two bright yellow cigar/disc shapes with dark bands
witnesses: Aurigny captain Ray Bowyer, passengers, a second pilot
summary: Flying an Aurigny Trislander from Southampton to Alderney, Capt. Ray Bowyer saw two very large, brilliant yellow objects apparently stationary over the sea, confirmed by passengers and by the pilot of another aircraft. He filed an official report with the Civil Aviation Authority.

title: Stephenville, Texas
explanation: The Air Force said F-16s from the 457th Fighter Squadron were training in the area. A MUFON analysis of FAA radar data claimed an untransponded target heading toward the Crawford ranch; this is not officially confirmed.
shape: Huge, silent, lit object up to a mile long
witnesses: ~40 residents incl. a pilot and a constable
summary: Dozens of people around Stephenville, including a private pilot and a local constable, reported a very large, silent object with bright lights followed by fighter jets. FOIA radar records later analysed by MUFON showed unidentified returns in the area.

title: Cláudio — Military Police report
shape: Luminous figures; lights in the sky
witnesses: 7 Military Police officers and residents
summary: Over the night of November 19–20, 2008, officers of the Minas Gerais Military Police said they chased luminous humanoid figures and photographed lights in the sky around the town of Cláudio. Seven officers signed the report, which includes three photographs and a police incident record.

title: Morristown lights (admitted hoax)
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: Hoax. Joe Rudy and Chris Russo tied road flares to helium balloons and released them on five nights, then revealed it on April 1, 2009 with video of the launches. They were fined for disorderly conduct.
shape: Five red lights in a line and arc
witnesses: Dozens of residents, police, Morristown Airport tower staff
summary: Around 8:15 p.m. on January 5, 2009, residents of Hanover Township, Morristown and nearby towns saw five red lights hanging in the sky and called 9-1-1. Tower staff at Morristown Airport also saw them, but radar showed nothing. TV news and UFO groups covered the lights, and they returned on four more nights. The two men who launched the balloons had also given TV interviews posing as witnesses. They called it a social experiment to show how unreliable eyewitness claims can be.

title: Norwegian spiral
place: Northern Norway and Sweden (seen from Troms and Finnmark)
explanation: A failed test of a Russian RSM-56 Bulava submarine-launched missile from the White Sea: the third stage malfunctioned, and the spinning missile sprayed fuel in a spiral lit by the Sun. The Russian Defence Ministry confirmed the failure the next day.
shape: Blue beam with an expanding white spiral
witnesses: Thousands across northern Norway and Sweden
summary: Before sunrise on December 9, 2009, people across northern Norway saw a blue-white light rise from behind the mountains, stop, and begin to spin. A glowing spiral grew outward and dissolved into a black hole-like disc. Photos and video went worldwide within hours. Astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell quickly suggested a failed Russian missile, and Moscow confirmed a Bulava test failure.

title: Hangzhou Xiaoshan Airport closure
explanation: Chinese UFO research groups found no radar images and concluded the object was probably an aircraft, possibly military.
shape: Bright object over the airport
witnesses: Airport staff and pilots
summary: A bright unidentified object above the airport led authorities to close Xiaoshan and divert flights for about an hour.

title: Aguadilla thermal video (DHS)
place: Rafael Hernández Airport, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: AARO assesses with high confidence the objects showed no anomalous speed or behaviour: a reconstruction of the sensor’s look angle shows two objects travelling near each other in a straight line at wind speed, never entering the water. Its case resolution assesses with moderate confidence that they were a pair of sky lanterns. Some independent analysts still dispute this.
shape: Small hot object; appears to enter and exit the sea
witnesses: U.S. Customs and Border Protection aircrew; tower controllers
summary: A Customs and Border Protection DHC-8 recorded a small, hot object crossing the airport and heading out over the ocean, where it appeared to plunge into the water and re-emerge. The leaked video became a staple of UAP analysis; AARO published a 3D reconstruction video in 2025.

title: Chilean Navy helicopter FLIR video
place: Coast between San Antonio and Quinteros, Chile
explanation: Chile’s aerial-phenomena office (CEFAA) left the case open because it could not be certain of the object’s nature. Later analyses by sceptics proposed an aircraft’s contrail and exhaust seen by infrared as the likely cause.
shape: Flat, elongated object with two hot discharges
witnesses: Navy helicopter crew (pilot and camera operator)
summary: On November 11, 2014 a Chilean Navy helicopter on coastal patrol west of Santiago, at about 4,500 feet, picked up an unknown object on its high-definition infrared camera. The two-man crew also saw it with the naked eye for more than ten minutes. The captain described a flat, elongated object with two thermal discharges that did not line up with its direction of travel, and the video shows what looks like a chemical plume. The Navy’s aerial-phenomena office CEFAA examined it and later released the footage, saying it could not be sure what it was. Sceptics later said the images match the contrail of a distant aircraft.

title: USS Theodore Roosevelt — Gimbal & GoFast
place: Atlantic warning areas off Jacksonville, Florida
explanation: Both videos were officially released and remain "unidentified" per DoD. Analysts such as Mick West argue GoFast shows a slow object (e.g. a balloon) at ~13,000 ft that only looks fast and low because of parallax, and that Gimbal’s rotation is a glare artifact of the ATFLIR pod. AARO later published a case resolution for GoFast worked out from the sensor’s geometry and the winds aloft.
evidence: video | sensor-data | radar | pilot-witness | military-witness | official-document
shape: Rotating lozenge (Gimbal); small fast object (GoFast)
witnesses: VFA-11 aircrew; Lt. Ryan Graves’ squadron reported near-daily objects
duration: Seconds of video; months of sightings
summary: In 2014–2015 F/A-18F crews of the Roosevelt strike group reported frequent unknown objects on their upgraded APG-79 radars off the East Coast. Two ATFLIR clips — "Gimbal", with a crew member exclaiming about "a whole fleet of them", and "GoFast", a small object skimming over the ocean — were released by the Pentagon in April 2020.

title: Ireland — airline pilots report fast lights
explanation: One pilot suggested a meteor or an object in re-entry, and an astronomer at the Armagh Observatory said the lights were most likely meteors. Air traffic control saw nothing on radar and no military exercises were running, so nothing has been confirmed.
shape: Very bright lights moving at high speed
witnesses: Crews of a British Airways and a Virgin Atlantic flight, and others
summary: At about 6:47 on the morning of November 9, 2018 the pilot of a British Airways flight from Montreal to London radioed Shannon air traffic control to ask whether military exercises were under way. A “very bright light” had come up on the left of the aircraft and “rapidly veered to the north”, then disappeared at very high speed. The crew of a Virgin Atlantic flight reported two bright lights that banked to the right and climbed away at what the pilot called “astronomical” speed, “like Mach 2”. Controllers saw nothing on radar, and no military exercises were taking place. The Irish Aviation Authority said it would investigate by confidentially interviewing the pilots. More than one crew reported it, and the story was carried by news outlets around the world.

title: USS Omaha sphere & USS Russell "pyramids"
explanation: The Pentagon confirmed the leaked clips were taken by Navy personnel. Analysts attribute the "pyramids" to the triangular aperture of a night-vision lens (bokeh) on aircraft/stars, and the Omaha sphere to a distant aircraft or balloon.
shape: Spherical object descending into the sea; flashing pyramid shapes
witnesses: Crew of USS Omaha, USS Russell and other ships
summary: During July 2019, several Navy ships off Southern California reported drone-like objects around them at night. A CIC video from USS Omaha shows a sphere flying over the ocean and apparently descending into the water; night-vision footage from USS Russell shows blinking pyramid-shaped lights. Both leaked in 2021 and were confirmed as authentic Navy footage.

title: Colorado and Nebraska drone swarms
place: Phillips County and the plains of north-eastern Colorado
explanation: State and federal agencies found that most reports were planets, stars, aircraft and hobby drones, and the Colorado Department of Public Safety stood its effort down in January 2020. The large, grid-flying drones of the first reports were never tied to an operator.
shape: Drones with a wingspan of about 6 ft and blinking lights, in groups of six to ten, flying grid patterns
witnesses: Ranchers, residents and county sheriff’s deputies
summary: In December 2019, residents and deputies in north-eastern Colorado and western Nebraska began reporting drones with wingspans of about six feet flying in groups of six to ten, at 200 to 500 feet, in grid patterns across the plains, mostly between about 7 and 10 p.m.; one witness counted 19. County sheriffs asked the public for information, and more than 70 local, state and federal agencies met in Brush on January 6, 2020. The FAA said no drone company or test site had authorized flights there, and the Air Force, which had run counter-drone exercises at F. E. Warren AFB, would neither claim nor deny the drones. As the sightings spread, more and more turned out to be planets, stars and airliners, and the state ended its search later that month.

title: American Airlines 2292 — “cruise-missile type of thing”
place: Northeastern New Mexico, at about 36,000 ft
explanation: No explanation has been given. The FAA said air traffic controllers saw no object on their radar. The Pentagon said the military was not conducting tests in the area that day, and the FBI said it was aware of the report.
shape: Long cylinder, “almost like a cruise missile”
witnesses: The crew of American Airlines Flight 2292
summary: On February 21, 2021, at about 12:29 p.m. local time, the crew of American Airlines Flight 2292, an Airbus A320 flying from Cincinnati to Phoenix at about 36,000 feet over the north-east corner of New Mexico, radioed: “Do you have any targets up here? We just had something go right over the top of us. I hate to say this, but it looked like a long cylindrical object that almost looked like a cruise missile type of thing, moving really fast right over the top of us.” The transmission was recorded by Steve Douglass, a radio listener. American Airlines at first denied that it was authentic, then confirmed that it was from Flight 2292 after talking to the crew. The FAA said controllers saw nothing on radar, and the Pentagon said it had no tests in the area.

title: Three objects on a Western U.S. military range
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: AARO matched the three dots to commercial airliners far from the infrared sensor using flight and radar data.
shape: Three small dots on infrared
witnesses: Range sensor operators
summary: Shown by AARO at NASA’s UAP Independent Study Team public meeting (May 31, 2023) as an example of a resolved case: three unidentified infrared dots turned out to be three separate commercial aircraft at great distance.

title: MQ-9 "Middle East orb"
explanation: AARO: the object did not show anomalous behaviour but remains unidentified for lack of data.
shape: Silver, orb-like object
witnesses: MQ-9 sensor operators
summary: Shown by AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick at the April 19, 2023 Senate Armed Services hearing: an MQ-9 Reaper’s sensor briefly tracks a silver orb crossing its field of view — typical of the many reports AARO receives with minimal data.

title: MQ-9 records object with "wake" — South Asia
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: AARO resolved the case in February 2024 (“Atmospheric Wakes”): frame-by-frame analysis and flight data showed a commuter aircraft flying near the two MQ-9s, and the apparent wake was the heat signature from its engines.
shape: Object with apparent atmospheric wake
witnesses: MQ-9 sensor operators
summary: An MQ-9 filming another MQ-9 caught an object with an apparent wake crossing the frame. AARO showed it at the April 2023 Senate hearing and released both clips.

title: Chinese surveillance balloon
explanation: A PRC high-altitude surveillance balloon; shot down by an F-22 AIM-9X off Surfside Beach, South Carolina, and recovered by the U.S. Navy.
shape: Large white balloon with solar-array payload
witnesses: Millions; NORAD tracking
summary: A high-altitude balloon from China crossed into U.S. airspace north of the Aleutians, drifted over Canada, passed over Malmstrom AFB in Montana and across the continent before being shot down off South Carolina. The event prompted NORAD to re-tune its radars, which led to the February 10–12 shoot-downs of three smaller unidentified objects.

title: February 2023 shoot-downs (Alaska, Yukon, Lake Huron)
explanation: The White House said the three objects were most likely benign commercial or research balloons; none was recovered. An infrared video of the Lake Huron shoot-down was released in 2026 as DOW-UAP-PR071.
shape: Small octagonal / cylindrical objects at 20,000–40,000 ft
witnesses: NORAD; F-22 and F-16 pilots
summary: After re-tuning radars following the Chinese balloon, NORAD detected and shot down three small objects in three days: off Deadhorse, Alaska (Feb 10), over central Yukon (Feb 11) and over Lake Huron (Feb 12). The first AIM-9X fired at the Lake Huron object missed. Debris was never recovered.

title: Colorado Springs law-enforcement videos
explanation: Released by AARO/PURSUE as unresolved reports from a local law-enforcement officer; no determination published.
shape: Silent lights flashing red, blue and green; triangle reports
witnesses: Local police officer; former DoW employee (FBI interview)
summary: The first local law-enforcement UAP files released by the U.S. government: cell-phone videos an officer submitted to AARO showing silent flashing lights, plus separate FBI interviews and renderings of triangle-shaped UAP seen over Colorado Springs in October 2023.

title: Imphal airport UFO — Rafales scrambled
place: Bir Tikendrajit International Airport, Imphal, Manipur
shape: Small white object
witnesses: Airport staff and officials
summary: An unidentified object seen near Imphal airport in the afternoon led the authorities to halt flights. Departures were delayed and arrivals diverted for about three hours. The Indian Air Force scrambled two Rafale fighters from a nearby base, which searched the area and found nothing. The object was not seen again.

title: Langley Air Force Base drone incursions
explanation: The Pentagon confirmed the incursions in October 2024 and said the drones did not appear to show hostile intent, but neither it nor NORAD has said who flew them.
shape: Drones of several sizes; the first reportedly about 20 ft long
witnesses: Base personnel and U.S. military officials
summary: From the evening of December 6, 2023, unauthorized drones flew over Langley Air Force Base, home of F-22 Raptor squadrons, across Hampton Roads from the Navy’s largest base at Norfolk, on and off for 17 days. The Wall Street Journal later reported that they typically arrived 45 minutes to an hour after sunset, that the first was about 20 feet long and flew at 3,000 to 4,000 feet, and that a dozen or more smaller drones followed. The Pentagon confirmed the incursions in October 2024. Gen. Glen VanHerck, who led NORAD at the time, later said the military had warned for years that it was not ready for this threat; he gave no new details about who was operating the drones.

title: Tyndall "Tic Tac" — USCG C-144
place: Southeastern U.S., near Tyndall AFB, Florida
explanation: AARO released the clips in 2026 as uploaded to a classified network, noting many of these records lack a substantiated chain of custody; no determination was made.
shape: "Tic Tac" — IR-hot area of contrast
witnesses: U.S. Coast Guard C-144 sensor operators
summary: Two infrared clips titled "USCG C-144 Tyndall UAP … TIC TAC IR hot 24 April 2024", likely from a Coast Guard HC-144 sensor over the Southeastern United States, released in PURSUE Release 02 in response to a House request.

title: New Jersey drone sightings
place: Morris County, New Jersey, and the Northeast
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: A joint FBI, DHS, FAA and DoD review found a mix of lawful commercial, hobbyist and law-enforcement drones, crewed aircraft and stars, with no threat to national security. In January 2025 the White House said the drones over New Jersey had been authorized by the FAA for research and other purposes.
shape: Large lighted drones; many reports were aircraft
witnesses: Thousands of residents, police, state officials
summary: From mid-November 2024, residents in Morris County reported large, lighted drones flying at night, including over Picatinny Arsenal and near the president-elect's golf club in Bedminster. Reports spread across New Jersey and into New York, Pennsylvania and beyond. The FAA placed temporary flight restrictions over dozens of sites. Stewart International Airport briefly closed its runways, and many viral videos turned out to show airliners.

title: Drones over the U.S. air bases in England
place: RAF Lakenheath, Mildenhall, Feltwell and Fairford, England
explanation: The U.S. Air Force and the Ministry of Defence confirmed the drones, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an investigation, but the operators were not identified.
shape: Small drones of varying number and type
witnesses: U.S. Air Force personnel; residents of nearby villages
summary: Between November 20 and 26, 2024, small drones were seen over and around four bases in England used by the U.S. Air Force: RAF Lakenheath, home of the 48th Fighter Wing, RAF Mildenhall, RAF Feltwell and RAF Fairford. The Air Force said “small unmanned aerial systems were spotted in the vicinity of and over RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall and RAF Feltwell between 20 and 22 November”. Air traffic into Mildenhall was disrupted: on November 21 a KC-46 tanker that had brought F-35s across the Atlantic turned back and diverted to Prestwick. British troops with counter-drone equipment were sent to help, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an inquiry. Similar reports came from U.S. bases in Germany that December.
